lines.cap: Your security clearance, part four: maintenance.
Alex is approved. Now the job is keeping the clearance in good standing.

scenes.label: Eligible is not the same as access

lines.cap: Now, let's say Alex is approved. Being eligible isn't the same as access.
Before seeing anything classified, Alex gets an initial security briefing and signs the SF 312, a nondisclosure agreement that lasts for life.
lines.say: Before seeing anything classified, Alex gets an initial security briefing and signs the S F three-twelve, a nondisclosure agreement that lasts for life.

lines.cap: The briefing covers threats, including insider threats, counterintelligence, how classification works, and your reporting duties.
And Alex only sees what the job requires. That's called need-to-know.
Every 12 months, you'll get refresher training.
A clearance isn't one and done. Cleared people are enrolled in continuous vetting, with automated record checks and an updated form about every five years.
That includes FBI Rap Back, which alerts DCSA to new criminal records in near real time.
Your part: report life changes to your FSO, like foreign travel and contacts, money trouble, or an arrest.
lines.say: Your part: report life changes to your F S O, like foreign travel and contacts, money trouble, or an arrest.

lines.cap: Before a personal trip abroad, give your FSO your itinerary. Report changes, and unplanned day trips to Canada or Mexico, within five business days of getting back.
lines.say: Before a personal trip abroad, give your F S O your itinerary. Report changes, and unplanned day trips to Canada or Mexico, within five business days of getting back.

lines.cap: Official travel for your government contract doesn't need to be reported.
Report close and continuing ties with foreign nationals, and any contact with someone you think may be a foreign intelligence officer.
Also report attempts to get classified information from you, an arrest, alcohol- or drug-related treatment, bankruptcy, or a debt more than 120 days past due.
Applying for foreign citizenship, using a foreign passport, and media contacts about classified matters are reportable too.
Top Secret holders report more, including marriage, cohabitation, foreign bank accounts or property, and voting in a foreign election.
And if you see reportable behavior by another cleared coworker, tell your FSO.
lines.say: And if you see reportable behavior by another cleared coworker, tell your F S O.

lines.cap: If you move to another cleared employer, your eligibility generally comes with you. Under federal reciprocity rules, your new FSO confirms it instead of starting over.
lines.say: If you move to another cleared employer, your eligibility generally comes with you. Under federal reciprocity rules, your new F S O confirms it instead of starting over.

lines.cap: When you leave, or no longer need access, your FSO debriefs you. Your SF 312 obligations never end.
lines.say: When you leave, or no longer need access, your F S O debriefs you. Your S F three-twelve obligations never end.

lines.cap: So: your FSO starts it. You complete eApp. DCSA reviews, investigates, and decides, with DOHA stepping in if there are issues.
lines.say: So: your F S O starts it. You complete e-App. DCSA reviews, investigates, and decides, with DOHA stepping in if there are issues.

lines.cap: Then you're briefed, you sign, and you keep reporting. Tell the truth, meet your deadlines, and talk to your FSO.
lines.say: Then you're briefed, you sign, and you keep reporting. Tell the truth, meet your deadlines, and talk to your F S O.
